# Fetch string-form request metadata is circular

## Context
A string-form Fetch request produces circular request metadata. It was captured while implementing `#19430` and independently triaged for promotion in [the #19435 review](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19435#pullrequestreview-5432072228). The URL-base fix is already approved; this ticket keeps the metadata repair separate.

## The Problem
At `14907a2bf3`, `Fetch.request(url, config)` assigns `config.url = config`. The returned `response.request` is that object, so `response.request.url === response.request` and JSON serialization throws. Object-form input for the same endpoint returns a string URL and serializes normally. A real Fetch instance with only native fetch stubbed confirmed identical dispatch and retained unrelated config keys in both forms. Native dispatch succeeds; the observed failure is metadata serialization.

## The Architectural Reality
Design authority: `Fetch.request` supports `Object|String` URL forms in its owning JSDoc and exposes the supplied request config through `response.request`. The current object-form path retains `config.url` as a string; the string-form branch contradicts that shape.

Prescription checked: `src/data/connection/Fetch.mjs#request` owns both input normalization and the returned metadata. No worker, Store, Pipeline or URL-base selector is needed.

## The Fix
Retain the original string URL in the supplied request config. Pin string/object-form metadata equivalence through the real Fetch API and its returned response; preserve native dispatch and the scoped URL resolver.

## Contract Ledger
| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback / Edge Case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Fetch.request` string input and `response.request.url` | Owning JSDoc and existing object-form path | The request URL remains the original string; request metadata serializes for ordinary serializable config | Preserve unrelated supplied config fields, object-form input and native response fields; do not rewrite metadata to the resolved/redirected response URL | Method JSDoc | Real connection tests with native fetch stub |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] String-form metadata contains the original URL string and serializes without a cycle introduced by Fetch.
- [ ] Equivalent object-form input retains its URL and unrelated config fields.
- [ ] Native URL dispatch and returned response data/status behavior remain unchanged; a workspace-relative case retains `#19430`'s resolver behavior.

## Out of Scope
Caller-supplied circular objects; header/body support; Stream/Xhr metadata; bare-relative URL expansion; document-base selection.
